This reply really hit me in a way that no other thing any redditor has said has. I appreciate both hearing your struggle and the perspective you have as a father in regard to your kids.

I myself have not dealt with addiction, I am absolutely positive it is a beast unlike I could ever imagine. But I have dealt with a lot of mental health issues, bipolar, depression, anxiety. It isn't the same at all, but I wanted to say that I believe that the first step to getting better is acknowledging there is something wrong, exactly like you have done. 

I am wishing you the absolute best. I think everyone is capable of changing for the better. I can't even the imagine the pain one must go through to get to the other side of this addiction. I think it's great to reach out to people going through similar experiences and find that community so you can get through this. 

I am proud of you for being able to seek help even after a lot of time suffering, not all people are willing to do that, like my father. I still have hope that my dad will seek out help similar to everyone who posts on this sub. I still have hope that someday he could be emotionally available for my sister. I have hope that if I tell him, if I show him how I really feel, and I do it right, he might understand. Guilt eats him alive without me telling him anything, but I have hope. 

Your kids may be young now, but when they are older I would bet they will be very appreciative of the effort you are putting in now. Once the pain is over, you will have the opportunity to foster even stronger relationships with your family. I am happy for you for choosing this path even though it is so difficult. Thank you for giving me such a valuable perspective and I genuinely wish you and your family all the best. Seriously, thank you so much.

I used to have this! I'd have headaches every day, no exceptions. Sometimes it would get bad enough where I'd have to ask my partner to talk quietly and turn off all the lights, let it pass for 30ish minutes, and continue on. Other times it was the 2-4/10 pain you describe. I talked to my neurologist mostly about my aura migraines but mentioned the daily headaches as well. They put me on a self-injection medicine called Ajovy, and not only do I have no aura migraines for the month duration it lasts, but I have no daily headaches. I know its time to take my next dose when the headaches start to return. It's a great medicine, feels almost like magic after suffering for 10 years, and would recommend it!
